content.name: Aisha Rahman
content.title: Junior DevOps Engineer
content.summary: Junior DevOps engineer who joined straight from A-levels through a Level 4 DevOps Engineer apprenticeship and passed the end-point assessment with distinction. Now looks after CI/CD and AWS infrastructure for an energy-software firm, where I automated test environments that used to take a day to build. Interested in observability and infrastructure as code.

experience.title: DevOps Engineer Apprentice (Level 4)
bullets: Containerised four internal Python services with Docker, so developers could run the full stack locally with one command.
Wrote GitLab CI pipelines that ran linting, tests and image scans on every merge request across six repositories.
Produced the apprenticeship portfolio around a real project, moving build agents to autoscaling runners that saved about £400 a month.

experience.title: Junior DevOps Engineer
bullets: Built Terraform modules for on-demand test environments, cutting set-up from roughly a day of manual work to 20 minutes.
Added Prometheus alerts and Grafana dashboards for the meter-data API, which spotted a memory leak before customers noticed.
Patched and rebuilt 30 EC2 instances during a critical OpenSSH vulnerability window within the 48-hour internal deadline.
Share on-call cover with two senior engineers during working hours and document each fix in the team runbook.

education.school: Steel City Tech Academy (apprenticeship training provider)

education.details: GCSEs: 9 subjects at grades 9–6, including Maths (8) and English Language (7).

achievements.title: Apprentice of the Year, Don Valley Energy Software
achievements.detail: Nominated by the engineering team for the test-environment automation work.

achievements.title: Volunteer, local Code Club
achievements.detail: Help run a weekly Scratch and Python club for 15 primary school children.
